item.text: {"case_id":"SHC004","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C15","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 is an earlier report on the same Libyan national emergency and supplies both distinctive language and the material reporting architecture reused by the child: identification of the prior report and statutory authorities, review of Libyan Sanctions Regulations and related Commerce/Transportation measures, licensing activity, enforcement, attributable federal expenses, and the concluding determination that Libya remains an unusual and extraordinary threat followed by promises to continue sanctions and periodic reporting. C15 and C08 are strong secondary analogues for the same sanctions-report structure, but concern Nicaragua rather than the child's Libyan reporting series.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I hereby report to the Congress on developments since my last report of July 8, 1988, concerning the national emergency with respect to Libya that was declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of January 7, 1986.","parent_excerpt":"I hereby report on developments since my last report of July 10, 1987, concerning the national emergency with respect to Libya that was declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of January 7, 1986.","explanation":"Nearly verbatim opening formula for the same emergency, updated only for the reporting period."},{"child_excerpt":"Since my last report on July 8, 1988, there have been no amendments to the Libyan Sanctions Regulations, 31 C.F.R. Part 550 (the \"Regulations\"), administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control","parent_excerpt":"Since my last report on July 10, 1987, there have been two amendments to the Libyan Sanctions Regulations, 31 C.F.R. Part 550 (the \"Regulations\"), administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control","explanation":"The child reuses the same regulation-status provision and terminology while substituting the new period's status."},{"child_excerpt":"During the current 6-month period, the Office has issued licenses to individuals and corporations to permit them to engage in activities that would otherwise be prohibited by the Regulations.","parent_excerpt":"The major licensing action occurring during the past 6 months under the Regulations involved blocked assets of the Libyan Arab Foreign Bank","explanation":"Both place a detailed account of OFAC licensing activity immediately after the regulatory update."},{"child_excerpt":"The expenses incurred by the Federal Government in the 6-month period from July 8, 1988, through the present time that are directly attributable to the exercise of powers and authorities conferred by the declaration of the Libyan national emergency are estimated at $461,745.","parent_excerpt":"The expenses incurred by the Federal Government in the 6-month period from July 10, 1987, through the present time that are directly attributable to the exercise of powers and authorities conferred by the declaration of the Libyan national emergency are estimated at $623,554.","explanation":"This is the same distinctive expense-reporting sentence with dates and amount updated."},{"child_excerpt":"The policies and actions of the Government of Libya continue to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States. I shall continue to exercise the powers at my disposal to apply economic sanctions against Libya as long as these measures are appropriate and will continue to report periodically to the Congress on significant developments","parent_excerpt":"The policies and actions of the Government of Libya continue to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States. I shall continue to exercise the powers at my disposal to apply economic sanctions against Libya as long as these measures are appropriate and will continue to report periodically to the Congress on significant developments","explanation":"The operative conclusion is reproduced essentially verbatim."}]}
